Niklas & Enquist Biomass Database — Detailed Summary

plant_scaling_data project

2026-05-01

1 Overview

The Niklas & Enquist biomass dataset is a cross-species compilation of plant biomass, height, age, and growth-rate measurements drawn from the primary literature, originally assembled by Enquist and Niklas as the empirical backbone for their metabolic scaling theory papers published in Nature and related journals (2001–2004). The primary published data compilation is described in:

Niklas KJ & Enquist BJ (2001). Invariant scaling relationships for interspecific plant biomass production rates and body size. PNAS, 98(5): 2922–2927. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.041590298

Enquist BJ & Niklas KJ (2002). Global allocation rules for patterns of biomass partitioning in seed plants. Science, 295: 1517–1520. DOI: 10.1126/science.1066360

The source CSV (niklas_enquist_biomass_20040122.csv) was compiled January 2004 and sourced from Cannell (1982) and other primary literature. Missing values are encoded as −999 in the original file and have been recoded to NA here.

⚠ Citation note: The citations above should be independently verified before use in any manuscript. DOIs have not been checked against Crossref in this exploratory summary.

n_rows  <- nrow(dat)
n_taxa  <- length(unique(dat$taxa))
n_cites <- length(unique(dat$citation))

kable(data.frame(
  Metric  = c("Total records", "Unique taxa strings", "Unique citations"),
  Value   = format(c(n_rows, n_taxa, n_cites), big.mark = ",")
), caption = "Top-level database summary")

2 Data structure

2.1 Column dictionary

col_dict <- data.frame(
  Column            = c("taxa","citation","footnotes","record_num",
                        "age_yr","height_m",
                        "root_biomass_kg","stem_biomass_kg","leaf_biomass_kg",
                        "shoot_biomass_kg","repro_biomass_kg","total_biomass_kg",
                        "stem_growth_kgyr","leaf_growth_kgyr",
                        "root_growth_kgyr","total_growth_kgyr"),
  Unit              = c("—","—","—","—",
                        "yr","m",
                        "kg dry wt","kg dry wt","kg dry wt",
                        "kg dry wt","kg dry wt","kg dry wt",
                        "kg yr⁻¹","kg yr⁻¹","kg yr⁻¹","kg yr⁻¹"),
  Description       = c("Taxon name (may include mixed stands)",
                        "Literature citation string",
                        "Footnotes from Cannell (1982) pages",
                        "Original sort order from source table",
                        "Plant age","Plant height",
                        "Root dry biomass per plant",
                        "Stem dry biomass per plant",
                        "Leaf dry biomass per plant",
                        "Shoot (stem+leaf) dry biomass per plant",
                        "Reproductive organ dry biomass",
                        "Total dry biomass (root+stem+leaf)",
                        "Annual stem dry mass increment",
                        "Annual leaf dry mass increment",
                        "Annual root dry mass increment",
                        "Annual total dry mass increment")
)
kable(col_dict, caption = "Column dictionary for Niklas-Enquist dataset")

2.2 Data availability per column

num_cols <- c("age_yr","height_m","root_biomass_kg","stem_biomass_kg",
              "leaf_biomass_kg","shoot_biomass_kg","repro_biomass_kg",
              "total_biomass_kg","stem_growth_kgyr","leaf_growth_kgyr",
              "root_growth_kgyr","total_growth_kgyr")

avail <- dat |>
  summarise(across(all_of(num_cols), ~ sum(!is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n") |>
  arrange(desc(n))

ggplot(avail, aes(x = reorder(variable, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2166ac") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Non-missing records",
       title = "Data availability per column",
       subtitle = paste0("Total rows = ", format(n_rows, big.mark = ",")))

rng <- dat |>
  summarise(across(all_of(num_cols),
    list(n = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
         min = ~ round(min(., na.rm = TRUE), 4),
         max = ~ round(max(., na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
    .names = "{.col}__{.fn}")) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
    names_to = c("variable", "stat"), names_sep = "__") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)

kable(rng, caption = "Non-missing counts and value ranges for numeric columns")

3.2 Taxa string composition

The dataset spans vascular plants including wild woody species, crops, and annual herbs. Taxon strings are free-text from the original publications and have not been harmonized to a taxonomic backbone in this exploratory summary.

# Rough classification by keywords
dat2 <- dat |>
  filter(!is.na(taxa)) |>
  mutate(likely_type = case_when(
    str_detect(taxa, regex("Pinus|Picea|Abies|Larix|Tsuga|Pseudotsuga|Cryptomeria|Chamaecyparis|Cedrus|Taxus", ignore_case=TRUE)) ~ "Conifer",
    str_detect(taxa, regex("wheat|barley|maize|corn|rice|soya|soybean|pea|bean|millet|oat|rye|cotton|sunflower|tobacco|potato", ignore_case=TRUE)) ~ "Crop/herb",
    str_detect(taxa, regex("Quercus|Fagus|Betula|Populus|Acer|Fraxinus|Alnus|Eucalyptus|Acacia", ignore_case=TRUE)) ~ "Broadleaf tree",
    TRUE ~ "Other / unclassified"
  ))

dat2 |>
  count(likely_type, sort = TRUE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(likely_type, n), y = n, fill = likely_type)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Records",
       title = "Rough functional group classification (keyword-based)",
       subtitle = "Formal taxonomy reconciliation required before analysis")

4 Age and size distributions

dat |> filter(!is.na(age_yr), age_yr > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_yr)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#4dac26", color = "white") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(x = "Age (yr, log scale)", y = "Count",
       title = paste0("Age distribution  (n = ", sum(!is.na(dat$age_yr) & dat$age_yr > 0), ")"))

dat |> filter(!is.na(height_m), height_m > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = height_m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#1b7837", color = "white") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(x = "Height (m, log scale)", y = "Count",
       title = paste0("Height distribution  (n = ", sum(!is.na(dat$height_m) & dat$height_m > 0), ")"))

5 Scaling relationships

All biomass variables are in kg dry weight per plant. Height is in m. Age is in yr. All regressions below are exploratory OLS on log10-transformed data. Standardized Major Axis (SMA) regression using smatr is required for unbiased allometric exponent estimation and will be applied in the formal analysis phase.

5.1 Total biomass vs. height

d1 <- dat |> filter(total_biomass_kg > 0, height_m > 0)
lm1 <- lm(log10(total_biomass_kg) ~ log10(height_m), data = d1)
b1 <- round(coef(lm1)[2], 3)
a1 <- round(10^coef(lm1)[1], 4)
n1 <- nrow(d1)

ggplot(d1, aes(x = height_m, y = total_biomass_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1, color = "#1b7837") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks() +
  labs(x = "Height (m)", y = "Total biomass (kg)",
       title = paste0("Total biomass ~ height  |  β = ", b1, "  |  n = ", format(n1, big.mark=",")))

OLS: total_biomass = 0.0646 × height^2.764 (n = 433).

5.2 Stem biomass vs. total biomass

d2 <- dat |> filter(stem_biomass_kg > 0, total_biomass_kg > 0)
lm2 <- lm(log10(stem_biomass_kg) ~ log10(total_biomass_kg), data = d2)
b2 <- round(coef(lm2)[2], 3); n2 <- nrow(d2)

ggplot(d2, aes(x = total_biomass_kg, y = stem_biomass_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1, color = "#2166ac") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks() +
  labs(x = "Total biomass (kg)", y = "Stem biomass (kg)",
       title = paste0("Stem ~ total biomass  |  β = ", b2, "  |  n = ", format(n2, big.mark=",")))

5.3 Leaf biomass vs. total biomass

d3 <- dat |> filter(leaf_biomass_kg > 0, total_biomass_kg > 0)
lm3 <- lm(log10(leaf_biomass_kg) ~ log10(total_biomass_kg), data = d3)
b3 <- round(coef(lm3)[2], 3); n3 <- nrow(d3)

ggplot(d3, aes(x = total_biomass_kg, y = leaf_biomass_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1, color = "#d6604d") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks() +
  labs(x = "Total biomass (kg)", y = "Leaf biomass (kg)",
       title = paste0("Leaf ~ total biomass  |  β = ", b3, "  |  n = ", format(n3, big.mark=",")))

5.4 Root biomass vs. total biomass

d4 <- dat |> filter(root_biomass_kg > 0, total_biomass_kg > 0)
lm4 <- lm(log10(root_biomass_kg) ~ log10(total_biomass_kg), data = d4)
b4 <- round(coef(lm4)[2], 3); n4 <- nrow(d4)

ggplot(d4, aes(x = total_biomass_kg, y = root_biomass_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1, color = "#762a83") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks() +
  labs(x = "Total biomass (kg)", y = "Root biomass (kg)",
       title = paste0("Root ~ total biomass  |  β = ", b4, "  |  n = ", format(n4, big.mark=",")))

5.5 Total growth rate vs. total biomass

d5 <- dat |> filter(total_growth_kgyr > 0, total_biomass_kg > 0)
lm5 <- lm(log10(total_growth_kgyr) ~ log10(total_biomass_kg), data = d5)
b5 <- round(coef(lm5)[2], 3); n5 <- nrow(d5)

ggplot(d5, aes(x = total_biomass_kg, y = total_growth_kgyr)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1, color = "#f4a582") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks() +
  labs(x = "Total biomass (kg)", y = "Total growth rate (kg yr⁻¹)",
       title = paste0("Growth rate ~ total biomass  |  β = ", b5, "  |  n = ", format(n5, big.mark=",")))

The WBE metabolic scaling prediction is β ≈ 0.75 for production ∝ biomass.

5.6 Summary of scaling exponents (exploratory OLS)

exponents <- data.frame(
  Relationship      = c("total_biomass ~ height",
                        "stem_biomass ~ total_biomass",
                        "leaf_biomass ~ total_biomass",
                        "root_biomass ~ total_biomass",
                        "total_growth ~ total_biomass"),
  OLS_beta          = c(b1, b2, b3, b4, b5),
  n                 = c(n1, n2, n3, n4, n5)
)
kable(exponents, caption = "Exploratory OLS scaling exponents (log10-log10). Use SMA for formal inference.")
Exploratory OLS scaling exponents (log10-log10). Use SMA for formal inference.
Relationship OLS_beta n
total_biomass ~ height 2.764 433
stem_biomass ~ total_biomass 1.088 664
leaf_biomass ~ total_biomass 0.806 658
root_biomass ~ total_biomass 0.967 664

7 Key caveats

  1. Taxon strings are unharmonized. Many entries are free-text names from Cannell (1982) and include mixed-stand descriptions, common names, and synonyms. Taxonomy reconciliation against a backbone (TPL, TNRS, or GBIF) is required before cross-dataset merging.

  2. Missing data sentinel. The original file uses −999 for missing values. These have been recoded to NA here; downstream scripts must not treat −999 as a valid observation.

  3. Crops and annuals. The dataset includes crop species (pearl millet, wheat, pea, soybean) alongside forest trees. Analyses of interspecific woody-plant scaling should filter on functional group or growth form.

  4. Shoot vs. total biomass. shoot_biomass_kg = stem + leaf (above-ground except reproduction). total_biomass_kg = root + stem + leaf. These must not be used interchangeably.

  5. Log columns. Pre-computed log10 columns are present in the source file but are derived quantities. The raw biomass columns should be used for independent analysis.

  6. OLS bias. All exponents reported here are OLS on log-transformed data. These underestimate true allometric exponents when both axes have error. Use SMA (smatr::sma()) for publication-quality inference.

  7. Citation verification required. The Niklas & Enquist (2001) and Enquist & Niklas (2002) references listed in the Overview need independent DOI and metadata verification before inclusion in any methods narrative.
